summary: API gateway adaptive-accept smoothing caused gradual accept-queue growth, upstream runtime swap and elevated 5xx
description:
Issue summary:
Customers started reporting elevated 5xx rates and long-tail latencies for short chat requests beginning ~2026-03-10 09:20 UTC. The initial signal was a persistent ~3-5% 5xx error rate for SpeedWrite (enterprise) on the chat and embeddings routes. Impact: production traffic in us-east experienced periodic spikes of 502/503 and long queuing before runtime handoff.

Impact:
- SpeedWrite experienced increased error rates on user-facing endpoints (chat generate and embeddings).
- Latency increased for short prompts (95p -> 1.2s to >3s).
- Some runtimes performed model-variant swaps and restarted, amplifying 5xx waves.

Environment:
- Hosted API (prod-us-east), mixed dedicated and ephemeral runtimes serving SpeedWrite tenant.
- Recent gateway smoothing configuration (adaptive accept queue smoothing) rolled to us-east on 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC (canary -> region rollout).

Initial hypothesis:
- Adaptive smoothing at api-gateway slowed accept-handshake rate under bursty small-payload traffic, causing accept-queue growth and longer runtime warmup. Runtimes hit prefetch backlog and triggered variant swap / GPU memory pressure leading to OOMs and restarts, returning 5xx to the client.

Requested action:
- Short-term mitigation to reduce customer errors and stabilize routing while infra investigates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send sustained high-frequency small chat requests (avg payload ~200 tokens) to /v1/chat/completions from us-east
2) Ensure request concurrency imitates tenant mix (mix of long-lived streaming and short stateless calls)
3) Observe gateway accept-queue length growth and rising P50/P95 latency after adaptive smoothing engages (~30-90s)
4) Monitor serving-runtime logs for prefetch backlog, model-variant swap events, and GPU memory warnings
logs: [2026-03-10T09:23:24Z] runtime: ERROR upstream: connection_reset_by_peer code=502 tid=0x7f9b
timeline: 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC - adaptive accept-queue smoothing rolled to us-east (canary completed)
2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - first customer alert from SpeedWrite CS (elevated 5xx, slow small requests)
2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - on-call SRE triage opened, initial mitigation applied (temporarily increased accept backlog limit)
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - observed multiple runtime variant swaps and GPU memory warnings correlating with 5xx waves
2026-03-10 11:15 UTC - rollback of region smoothing config to previous thresholds (partial mitig)
investigation_notes: Checked deployment history: smoothing PR (runtime/gateway PR#2483) introduced rate damping to reduce transient over-accept during noisy bursts.
Observed that smoothing engaged aggressively for sequences dominated by short requests; the damping reduced accept throughput below runtime prefetch steady-state, causing prefetch backlog to grow.

Prefetch backlog caused model-variant swap logic to trigger (prefetch wait timeout), which initiated a variant fallback reload sequence that incurred GPU memory allocations; several GPUs showed fragmentation and temporally increased resident set leading to OOM watchdog restarts on some ephemeral nodes.
Runtime logs indicate variant swap and model reloads happened concurrently across multiple ephemeral workers, amplifying pressure on the cluster's NVMe and GPU memory subsystems.
No evidence of application-level model bugs; primary root appears to be interaction between gateway smoothing parameters and runtime prefetch/variant-swap heuristics.
Correlation with linked issues: SUP-472901 had similar symptom pattern from earlier keystore/preload thrash; takeaways applied.
Temporary fix reduced error rate but not back to baseline; need configuration + runtime debounce change to prevent swap storms.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC - Initial reply to SpeedWrite CS acknowledging elevated errors and that engineering is investigating (Aisha)
2026-03-10 10:10 UTC - Notified SpeedWrite of mitigation steps (increased accept backlog, rolling rollback of smoothing) and asked for any specific client retry patterns
2026-03-10 11:45 UTC - Follow-up status: partial relief after rollback, monitoring; asked for logs if they still see errors
actions_taken: Raised accept backlog and temporarily disabled aggressive smoothing for us-east
Initiated rolling rollback of gateway smoothing config to previous stable thresholds (2026-03-10 11:00 UTC)
Batched runtime restarts staged to avoid simultaneous variant reloads; coordinated with scheduler to stagger ephemeral worker restarts
Added temporary telemetry dashboards to track prefetch backlog, variant-swap rate, and GPU memory fragmentation
next_steps: Infra: implement a runtime debounce that prevents concurrent variant-swap reloads across workers on the same shard
Gateway: update adaptive smoothing to consider runtime prefetch occupancy metric before damping accept rate
Product/RE: confirm acceptable smoothing thresholds for mixed short/long request mixes (A/B test plan)
Postmortem: create incident postmortem and update runbook with new checks (owner: Marco)
Customer: follow up with SpeedWrite when baseline confirmed and offer 1:1 engagement during next release
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-10 09:36]: Acknowledged to customer, opened ticket and escalated to on-call SRE.
SRE-oncall (Lina Chen) [2026-03-10 09:42]: Initial triage - accept-queue in gateway showing smoothing hysteresis; disabling smoothing for region to confirm.
Marco Ruiz (Infra) [2026-03-10 10:02]: Increased accept backlog limit; noticed runtime prefetch backlog correlate with 5xx bursts; preparing rollback plan for smoothing PR.
Lina Chen (SRE) [2026-03-10 11:12]: Performed rollback of smoothing thresholds at 11:00 UTC; 5xx rate dropped from 4.2% -> 0.8% in 10m.
Marco Ruiz (Infra) [2026-03-11 08:10]: Suggested long-term: add gating in gateway that queries runtime prefetch metric (or schedules accept ramp) before applying dampening.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied (rollback of smoothing thresholds + increased accept backlog) which reduced 5xx to near baseline. Root cause: unsafe interaction between api-gateway adaptive smoothing and runtime prefetch/variant-swap heuristics causing synchronized variant reloads and GPU memory pressure. Next: implement runtime debounce and gating in gateway before re-enabling smoothing. Postmortem and permanent fixes planned.
